net: TCP / UDP / Unix Sockets and HTTP/2

This page outlines five networking contracts: net.sai (sockets and addresses), netx.sai (the io_uring reactor), http2.sai (HTTP/2 client and protocol tools), tls_client.sai (TLS client) and ws_client.sai (WebSocket client). After reading it, you will be able to choose the right level at which to initiate a TCP/TLS/WebSocket connection or write a listening service.

net.sai: Sockets

TcpStream, TcpListener, UdpSocket and NetAddr are all opaque u64 handles. Representative functions:

SignatureDescription
sa_std_net_tcp_connect(&host: ptr, host_len: u64, port: u32, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32TCP connection; there are also _timeout/_timeout_all variants
sa_std_net_tcp_listen(&host, host_len, port: u32, &out_handle, &out_bound_port: ptr) -> i32Listen; when the port is 0, the actual bound port is filled in
sa_std_net_tcp_accept(listener: u64, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32 / _accept_addr(...)Accept a connection, optionally also obtaining the peer address
sa_std_net_tcp_stream_read(stream: u64, &buf: ptr, cap: u64, &out_read: ptr) -> i32 / _write(...)Stream reading/writing; there are also peek and vectored variants
sa_std_net_tcp_stream_set_nodelay(stream: u64, enabled: i32) -> i32TCP_NODELAY; similar options include keepalive, TTL, buffer sizes, linger, non-blocking, etc.
sa_std_net_udp_bind(&host, host_len, port: u32, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Bind UDP; accompanied by send/recv/send_to/recv_from/peek_from and multicast options
sa_std_net_unix_listen/_connect/_pair(&path..., &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Unix domain sockets; handles reuse the tcp_stream/tcp_listener kinds
sa_net_addr_host(addr: u64) -> &ptr / _host_len / _port / _family + sa_net_addr_free(addr: u64) -> i32!Accessing and releasing an owned address object
sa_std_url_parse(&url: ptr, url_len: u64, ...12 参数...) -> i32Parse scheme://host[:port][/path]; any out buffer may be omitted
sa_std_ws_frame_parse(...) -> i32 / sa_std_ws_frame_build_unmasked(opcode: u32, fin: u32, ...) -> i32 / sa_std_ws_accept_key(...)Shared WebSocket frame codec and handshake key
sa_std_last_error() -> i32 / sa_std_net_error_code_name(code: i32, &out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32The most recent error code and its name

There is also a simplified sa_net_* surface (such as sa_net_tcp_connect(&host: ptr, host_len: u64, port: u32) -> u64!, sa_net_tcp_stream_write_all(stream: u64, &buf: ptr, len: u64) -> i32!, sa_net_tcp_listener_bind(&host: ptr, host_len: u64, port: u16) -> u64!), which returns fallible handles and suits script-style use.

netx.sai: The io_uring Reactor

The runtime hosts the sockets, slot pool and io_uring orchestration, and all entry points return a plain i32 status code (SA_NETX_OK / SA_NETX_ERR_*):

SignatureDescription
sa_netx_init(slot_capacity: u64, reactor_count: u32) -> i32Initialize the reactor pool
sa_netx_listen(&host: ptr, host_len: u64, port: u16) -> i32Register a listener
sa_netx_recv_ticket(reactor_id: u32, &out_ticket: ptr) -> i32Claim a receive ticket
sa_netx_push_outbound(reactor_id: u32, slot_id: u32, &msg: ptr, len: u32) -> i32Push an outbound message to a slot
sa_netx_broadcast(reactor_id: u32, &slot_ids: ptr, n: u32, &msg: ptr, len: u32) -> i32Broadcast to multiple slots
sa_netx_close_slot(slot_id: u32) -> i32 / sa_netx_shutdown() -> i32Close a slot / shut down entirely

http2.sai: HTTP/2

SignatureDescription
sa_std_http2_supported(&out_supported: ptr) -> i32Whether the backend is available (libnghttp2)
sa_std_http2_client_request(&url: ptr, url_len: u64, &method: ptr, method_len: u64, &body: ptr, body_len: u64, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Initiate an HTTP/2 request; the result is a buffer handle
sa_std_http2_get_packed_settings(&settings_json: ptr, settings_json_len: u64, &out_handle: ptr) -> i32Generate a packed SETTINGS frame from JSON settings; _get_unpacked_settings_json is the reverse
sa_std_http2_perform_server_handshake(&input: ptr, input_len: u64, &settings_json: ptr, settings_json_len: u64, &out_bytes: ptr, &out_json: ptr) -> i32Server-side handshake processing
sa_std_http2_buffer_data(buffer: u64) -> &ptr / _len / _free(^buffer: u64) -> i32The result-buffer trio
NoteAn address object (NetAddr) is an owned value, and sa_net_addr_free must be called after you have finished accessing it; the JA3/JA4 fingerprint digest functions (sa_std_net_ja3_hash, etc.) are also in this contract.

tls_client.sai / ws_client.sai: TLS and WebSocket Clients

Application-layer outbound encryption and WebSocket capability have been moved down from plugins into sa_std, in a pure Zig implementation with no native library dependencies. See the dedicated pages for details:

  • tls_client.sai: TLS client. connect() completes TCP dialing + handshake in one go, with verification always on (SNI + hostname checking + system CA), and no switch to turn it off; the error codes include -100 (certificate verification failure).
  • ws_client.sai: RFC 6455 WebSocket client. ws:// connects directly, wss:// reuses sa_tls_client; client frames are forcibly masked, fragments are automatically reassembled, pings are automatically answered with pongs, and on a protocol violation recv() returns -5.

IPv6 works out of the box ([::1]:port has been measured). HTTP/3 still has only a capability-probing skeleton (sa_quic.zig), and an SSH client has not yet been implemented — see Current Limitations and Roadmap Status.
